title.narrative: Emergency cholera response and prevention in Gedaref state, Sudan

description.narrative: ltpgtGedaref state is one of the most-affected state by the ongoing cholera outbreak declared in Sudan in August 2024. With 4,363 reported cases and 149 associated deaths, it accounts for 23% of the total 18,961 reported cases as of October 1st, and 555 associated deaths. The state’s 3.4% Case Fatality Rate (CFR), above the country’s overall 2.9 CFR, and 14.11/10,000 attack rate, evidence that, while the disease is rapidly spreading, access to treatment is poor and needs to be immediately enhanced. The state currently hosts 951,178 internally displaced persons (IDPs), living in deteriorated sanitary and hygiene conditions with poor access to clean water, and placing significant strain on overwhelmed, poorly equipped health facilities lacking specifically trained staff. ltbrgt ltbrgtPUI proposed intervention's objective is to contribute to the reduction of mortality and morbidity of the most vulnerable, IDPs and host communities, in Gedaref state’s most-affected three localities by the cholera outbreak, namely Baladiat al Gedaref, Al Fao and Al Fashaga, by focusing on a three-fold lifesaving health response: ltbrgt ltbgt1) Improve and ensure access to prompt and appropriate medical treatment lt/bgt ltbrgtIn Al Fao locality, which shares a border with Al Jazirah state, and where there is a need for two isolation centers, PUI will establish and support two CTUs in Village 10 and Village 5, consisting of two separated areas each, dedicated respectively to the treatment of severe AWD / cholera cases, and the treatment of mild AWD cases, as well as community awareness in a delimited space. ltbrgtFrom May 2025, PUI will focus on six ORPs in Baladiyat Gedaref and their corresponding ORPs, in accordance with the request from MOH.ltbrgtPUI will also support the maintenance of 2 MoH Ambulances in Baladiyat Gedaref. . ltbrgt ltbrgtltbgt2) Enhance surveillance and case reporting at HF and community levelslt/bgt ltbrgtAt the HF level, Aleshraq will coordinate with the SMoH for the training of all SMoH staff operating in the supported structures on Cholera Case Management, IPC and Outbreak Preparedness and Response, while PUI and Aleshraq will provide on-the-job capacity-building through their technical staff. ltbrgtAt the community level, in each supported CTU’s and ORC’s catchment areas, Aleshraq will establish one Community Outbreak Response Team (CORT), composed of 10 trained Community-Based Surveillance Officers (CBSOs), to ensure the early detection of any new suspected cholera case and help control and prevent the spread of the outbreak. In coordination with PUI, Aleshraq will collaborate with WaSH partners and the SMoH to facilitate the disinfection of contaminated households. ltbrgt ltbrgtltbgt3) Implement effective communication and community engagement to prevent and control the spread of choleralt/bgtlt/pgtltpgtThe CORTs established by Aleshraq will also be in charge of raising awareness among the community on several topics, such as cholera prevention and detection, disinfection of contaminated areas and hygiene promotion messages. Additionally, messages on cholera prevention will be disseminated by the nurses from the ORCs’ awareness-raising corners to patients when they are gathered in the waiting room, awaiting consultations. ltbrgt ltbrgtThis project will complement / be complemented by the WaSH response SHF’s pre-identified partner CARE will implement in the same targeted areas. ltbrgt ltbrgtThrough the proposed intervention, a total of 990 patients will be treated for AWD, including cholera, across Gedaref state’s three targeted localities, and 135 referred for higher level of care. 120 CBSOs will be deployed and a total of 52 healthcare staff trained. ltbrgtlt/pgt
